subject: hammerhead worm
title: This Garden Worm Carries Pufferfish Poison, and It Hunts Earthworms

scenes.text: This worm carries pufferfish poison. It may be in your garden.
The hammerhead worm grows up to a foot long, with a head shaped like a shovel.
It came from Southeast Asia, and reached the United States by 1901.
It doesn't eat plants. It hunts earthworms, slugs, even other hammerhead worms.
In 2014 scientists found what it carries: tetrodotoxin, the nerve poison of pufferfish, likely used to subdue prey.
It was the first time that toxin had turned up in any land invertebrate.

description:
Hammerhead worms are land flatworms from Southeast Asia that can reach a foot in length, and they carry the same nerve poison as pufferfish.
A 2014 study in PLOS ONE found tetrodotoxin in two species, Bipalium adventitium and Bipalium kewense: the first time the toxin had been found in a land invertebrate. The worms prey on earthworms, slugs and each other, and the toxin is thought to help subdue large earthworms and to protect the worm and its egg capsules. Reports of them in the United States go back to 1901. Little is known about the toxin's effect on people, so gardeners are told not to handle them bare-handed.
Have you ever seen one? Comment below.
first_comment: The toxin was also found in its egg capsules, so it may protect the next generation too. Have you ever found one of these in your garden?
